description:
Program Overview

The Clarendon Scholarship is the University of Oxford's flagship graduate scholarship scheme, offering over 200 new scholarships every year to academically excellent students from around the world. These scholarships cover full tuition and living costs for graduate study in Computer Science or AI-related fields at Oxford.

Funding & Benefits

  • Full Course Fees: Complete coverage at the international rate for entire course duration
  • Living Cost Grant: at least the UKRI minimum doctoral stipend rate (£21,805 per year, 2026-27 rate)
  • Research Allowance: Up to £1,000 per year for research expenses
  • Thesis Grant: £500 for thesis production costs
  • Travel Allowance: Up to £500 for conference travel

Eligibility Criteria

  • Academic Excellence: Outstanding academic record (typically first-class honours or equivalent)
  • Nationality: Open to all nationalities (UK and international students)
  • Course Requirements: Must apply for a full-time or part-time graduate course at Oxford
  • Research Potential: Demonstrated research aptitude for doctoral programs
  • English Language: Standard Oxford requirements (IELTS 7.0+ or equivalent)

Application Process

No separate scholarship application! All eligible applicants to Oxford graduate courses are automatically considered for Clarendon Scholarships.

  1. Apply to Oxford course through Graduate Application
  2. Submit research proposal (1,000-word for doctoral programs)
  3. Provide academic transcripts and three academic references
  4. CV/Resume highlighting research experience
  5. Departmental nomination
  6. Clarendon Fund selection
  7. Award notification (March-April 2027)

Timeline & Deadlines

StageDate
Application OpensSeptember 2026
December DeadlineJanuary 2027 (most courses)
March DeadlineMarch 2027 (some remaining courses)
Award NotificationMarch-April 2027

Official Link

https://www.ox.ac.uk/clarendon

Important Notes

  • No additional application required - automatically considered when applying to Oxford.
  • Oxford is ranked #1 in the world for Computer Science (QS 2027).
  • Focus on crafting an exceptional course application with a strong research proposal.
